behaviour-verdict-v1.json.description: A behaviour verdict definition (ENH-006 G19, operator decisions G19-1 to G19-6 of 2026-11-08, revising D9): what miServer serves as ONE verdict for a behaviour's probe stack, BESIDE the member results, which are unchanged. Exported by miWorkbench from one candidate of a stored blend report (041) with the report's RECORDED parameters; written as RFC 8785 (JCS) after rounding every float to 6 decimals, so two exports of one report are byte-identical. SEMANTICS (pinned by behaviour-verdict-cases.json; per behaviour and window): (1) rule match (any `rules.match.any_of` expression true after the vetoes) -> fires true, decided_by rule_match; a match beats a veto. (2) rule veto (a veto removed a span and nothing matched) suppresses the members whose `veto_applies` is true. (3) the candidate over the members not suppressed: any_of / all_of / k_of_n count members whose OWN served verdict fired, fires when the count >= k (no bar of its own); stack / max / best_single standardise each member's score with params.mean and params.std, then stack = intercept + sum(weights * z), max = max(z), best_single = z[member_index], and fire when value >= threshold (no length bands). (4) an unknown rule (timeout, error, pending operator code, the rule set absent) is no match and no veto; the members decide. (5) a member not armed or that produced nothing: fires true only when a rule or a present member proves it, otherwise fires null with decided_by members_missing, never false. A verdict false while the veto held reads decided_by vetoed. Members bind by detector digest; members_digest = sha256 of the JCS of the sorted detector digests. A consumer recomputes every combiner vector at attach and refuses on any disagreement (value within 1e-9, everything else exact).

CalibrationProbe.description:
One falsifiable correctness probe used to find the cliff (IDL-37).

Deliberately a NEUTRAL factual question — a topic the circuit should NOT
influence — so that degradation shows up as the circuit's tint corrupting an
unrelated fact (detectable), rather than as a change to output on the
circuit's own concept (whose "right answer" is not falsifiable). The probe
travels in the contract so a serve-time re-verify is one cheap pass.

CircuitCalibration.description:
Calibrated usable-strength band for the circuit's serving dial (IDL-37).

Badge, not gate. When present, its `[onset, cliff]` is what
`CircuitBudget.intensity_range` is clamped to (a served dial cannot reach
the nonsense zone) and `sweet_spot` is the default `intensity`.

`provisional` is True whenever the probes were GENERATED (not authored) or
the band was measured on the discovery-plane model rather than re-verified
against the served model — an honest confidence marker, never a blocker.

cliff.description: max dial still correct; above this the judge flips to broken

onset.description: min dial with influence above baseline noise

sweet_spot.description: usable dial: strongest still-correct point, with margin

What the probe detects, as miWorkbench's behaviour catalogue names it (Feature 037, D23).

* `key` — the behaviour's slug (`<behaviour-key>`). miServer groups verdicts by it (D18).
* `name` — the catalogue's name at export; for a key that is not catalogued, the probe's own
  behaviour label, or the key itself.
* `version` — the catalogue definition version current at export, or `null` when the key is not

No lifecycle flag (D50): miServer groups by key and does not need to know a behaviour was
archived.

BosHandling.description:
What the start-of-text (BOS) rule did when the producer tokenized its renders.

⚠ ADDITIVE AND OPTIONAL (2026-10-08, finding F1). miServer tokenizes a chat render with
`add_special_tokens=False` only when the render already begins with the tokenizer's BOS text,
and lets the tokenizer add its specials otherwise — so exactly one BOS when the model uses
one, never a duplicate. miWorkbench adopted that rule on this date; before it, it ALWAYS passed
False, which differs on one form: a template that writes no BOS while its tokenizer adds one
(TinyLlama-Chat / Zephyr-style), where miServer serves one BOS and miWorkbench trained on none.

Measured from the ids on the producer's tokenizer, never inferred from the flags.

DerivedFrom.description:

⚠ OUTSIDE BOTH DIGESTS (CHAIN_PLAN P25). `provenance` is excluded by name from the detector projection and is not
part of the decision projection, so this lineage never moves a digest: a patched head is a new detector by its
tensors, and a re-evaluated verdict or an upgraded provider must not change identity.

Evidence.description:
What is actually known about this probe — the expensive part of the document.

⚠ `rung_language` IS CARRIED, NOT RECOMPUTED BY THE CONSUMER. The wording that describes a
rung is the product's claim about it, and 033's whole purpose is that miServer can refuse to
serve a probe whose claim is weaker than the use. A consumer inventing its own phrasing is a
second source of truth for a causal statement.

LengthBand.description:
An operating point for ONE band of input lengths, in ABSOLUTE token counts.

⚠ ONE CONSTANT THRESHOLD IS MISCALIBRATED AT EVERY LENGTH BUT THE ONE IT WAS CUT AT. A
probe's score drifts with how many tokens were scored, in a direction that depends on the
corpus. Measured on a `mean` probe over five out-of-distribution sets: realised FPR
reaching 5.4x its 1% budget on the longest quartile of one set, and recall falling
0.500 -> 0.297 on another — the direction that takes a monitor silent as a conversation
grows. Correcting for length recovered +0.039 mean OOD AUROC against null controls that
all came back negative.

⚠ `max_tokens: None` MEANS OPEN-ENDED, AND THE LAST BAND MUST BE. A consumer sees one
request at a time; a table that stops short would leave the longest inputs with no bar at
all, which is precisely the regime the drift makes worst.

⚠ `threshold_source` DISTINGUISHES A CUT BAR FROM AN INHERITED ONE. Placing a `target_fpr`
quantile needs at least `1/target_fpr` negatives — 100 at 1%. A band below that carries
`"global"` and the document's single threshold, rather than a number computed from four
samples. A reader must be able to tell which bands were actually measured.

ModelIdentity.description:
Which model's activations this probe reads, pinned hard enough to serve against.

⚠ `revision` IS A RESOLVED COMMIT SHA, NOT A BRANCH. "main" moves, and a probe read from a
different revision of the same repo is a probe over a different distribution — the estate has
already paid for that once at the tokenizer level, where two models sharing a family name
agreed on 0.00% of token ids.

⚠ `chat_template_sha256` IS PART OF THE IDENTITY. The role mask and every rendered row depend
on the template. A model whose template changed renders different text from the same messages,
so a consumer must be able to notice.

ProbeHead.description:
The readout: `w`, `b`, and the standardisation it was FITTED with.

⚠ THE NORMALISATION TRAVELS WITH THE WEIGHTS BECAUSE IT IS PART OF THE FUNCTION. A head
applied to unstandardised activations is not a worse probe, it is a different one — the same
wrong-basis class as encoding with an SAE's normalisation dropped (MIS-E2E-083).

ProbeIdentity.description:
Which detector and which bar this document is (Feature 039, BR-025).

* `detector_digest` — SHA-256 of the canonical DETECTOR projection: the model, the read point,
  the head, the SAE basis, the combining rule and the render form. Equal across a re-cut of
  the bar; that is what lets a consumer see "same detector, new threshold".
* `decision_digest` — SHA-256 of the canonical `decision` block, every key present.
* `decision_revision` — miWorkbench's revision of the bar (the highest `revision` in the probe's
  calibration history, 1 when none). Not derivable from the document, so not checked by it.

Both digests are RECOMPUTED by the contract's validator whenever this block is present
(`probe_identity.check_identity`), so a document carrying a wrong digest is refused rather than
trusted. How they are computed is frozen by `docs/schemas/probe-identity-cases.json`.

⚠ INTEGRITY, NOT AUTHENTICITY. A digest proves the document agrees with itself, not who made it.

`None` (the block absent) means NOT RECORDED: the document was built before Feature 039.

ReadPoint.description:
⚠ `hook_point` IS A Literal WITH ONE MEMBER, AND THAT IS THE POINT.

This estate captured at a post-attention norm for months while every document said
"residual", and nothing could tell: the numbers were plausible and the SAEs trained fine on a
signal miServer never reads. A single-member Literal means a document claiming any other capture
point is refused rather than interpreted.

RenderForm.description:
How the producer turned a conversation into the token ids it trained and scored on.

⚠ ADDITIVE AND OPTIONAL (2026-10-08). miServer scores a live chat with the model's GENERATION
PROMPT after the last user turn; miWorkbench rendered without it until this date, so every probe
built before it was calibrated on a form it never sees live (measured on production: AUROC
0.9558 served against 0.9420 without the prompt). Since then miWorkbench renders exactly as
miServer serves:

  * `generation_prompt: true` — a conversation that does not end on an assistant turn
    (including plain prose, rendered as one user turn) carries the generation prompt, and
    every position is prompt. An assistant-ended conversation is rendered WITHOUT it, its
    prompt/response boundary at the render of the preceding turns WITH it.
  * `add_special_tokens` — what was passed to the tokenizer. With `bos_handling` present it
    follows miServer's start-of-text rule: `false` when the template writes the BOS, `true`
    otherwise (the tokenizer adds exactly what it adds by default).
  * `bos_handling` — what that rule produced (see `BosHandling`).

⚠ `bos_handling` ABSENT MEANS NOT RECORDED, NEVER "the tokenizer added one". A document
without it was built under the earlier rule, `add_special_tokens: false` for every model, and
still means exactly that; its ids equal the start-of-text rule's only when the model's
template writes the BOS or its tokenizer adds nothing, which a consumer can check against the
tokenizer but must not assume.

The block ABSENT means NOT RECORDED — the document predates the field, and for miWorkbench that
means rendered WITHOUT the generation prompt. It must never be read as the served form. A
consumer may warn on an absent block; it may not treat it as recorded.

SaeReference.description:
Where the SAE lives and exactly how it normalises — required for `sae_features`.

⚠ `normalization` IS NOT DECORATION. `encode_with_training_normalization` exists because
encoding with a bare `encode()` reads the right weights in the wrong basis, produces
plausible features and is invisible in the numbers. A consumer that cannot reproduce the
normalisation cannot reproduce the probe.

TestVector.description:
One row scored by the exporting build, for a consumer to reproduce.

⚠ `token_scores` HAS ONE ENTRY PER SCORED TOKEN, NOT PER TOKEN. The scope decides which
tokens are scored; a consumer comparing a full-length score array against its own masked one
would disagree for a reason that has nothing to do with the weights.

TestVectors.description:
The parity set, with the tolerance the producer suggests comparing at.

⚠ SCORE `token_ids`. NOT `messages`. THIS IS NOT A PREFERENCE.

Measured in 033 acceptance 8.1 on a real definition, 16 vectors:

    scored from the recorded `token_ids`   max |Δ| = 0.000e+00   (exact, all 16)
    re-rendered from `messages`            max |Δ| = 1.153e+00   (23x the tolerance)

`messages` is a **reconstruction**. The training corpus here is plain prose, not conversations,
so the exporter wraps each row in a single user turn to have something a consumer can send —
and re-rendering that through the model's chat template adds six tokens of scaffolding the
scored row never had, with the first difference at index 2. Two of the sixteen rows were
truncated to the token cap, keeping the TAIL, so their re-render differs from index 0.

A consumer that took `messages`, scored them and compared against `score` within `tolerance`
would fail on **every vector** and conclude its implementation was wrong. A parity check exists
to tell a correct implementation from an incorrect one; one that reports "incorrect" against a
correct implementation is worse than no check at all, because it is believed once.

`messages_reproduce_token_ids` is measured at build time — the exporter re-renders its own
`messages` and compares — so a consumer is told whether it may start from them rather than
finding out from a failed comparison.

WindowDecision.description:
An operating point for ONE window, cut from that window's own negatives.

⚠ A THRESHOLD IS A QUANTILE OF ONE WINDOW'S NEGATIVES. A consumer may read the same weights
over the prompt alone or the response alone — the prompt says something about the user, the
response about the model — and over a different window the top-level `threshold` no longer
names the same false-positive rate, because it is a quantile of a different distribution. A
verdict judged against the wrong one is a ranking, not a rate.

`scope` records which of the producer's INTERNAL scopes this window was cut under, so a reader
can tell what `prompt` meant here without re-deriving anyone's mapping. It matters: the
contract's `prompt` is positional, `[0, n_prompt)`, which includes a system preamble and every
earlier assistant turn — a producer that calibrated a role-based "user" mask has cut a bar for
a narrower window than the consumer reads, and this field is where that shows.

behaviour-verdict-v1.json.description: A behaviour verdict definition (ENH-006 G19, operator decisions G19-1 to G19-6 of 2026-11-08, revising D9): what miServer serves as ONE verdict for a behaviour's probe stack, BESIDE the member results, which are unchanged. Exported by miWorkbench from one candidate of a stored blend report (041) with the report's RECORDED parameters; written as RFC 8785 (JCS) after rounding every float to 6 decimals, so two exports of one report are byte-identical. SEMANTICS (pinned by behaviour-verdict-cases.json; per behaviour and window): (1) rule match (any `rules.match.any_of` expression true after the vetoes) -> fires true, decided_by rule_match; a match beats a veto. (2) rule veto (a veto removed a span and nothing matched) suppresses the members whose `veto_applies` is true. (3) the candidate over the members not suppressed: any_of / all_of / k_of_n count members whose OWN served verdict fired, fires when the count >= k (no bar of its own); stack / max / best_single standardise each member's score with params.mean and params.std, then stack = intercept + sum(weights * z), max = max(z), best_single = z[member_index], and fire when value >= threshold (no length bands). (4) an unknown rule (timeout, error, pending operator code, the rule set absent) is no match and no veto; the members decide. (5) a member not armed or that produced nothing: fires true only when a rule or a present member proves it, otherwise fires null with decided_by members_missing, never false. A verdict false while the veto held reads decided_by vetoed. Members bind by detector digest; members_digest = sha256 of the JCS of the sorted detector digests. behaviour-verdict-v1.json.description: A behaviour verdict definition (ENH-006 G19, operator decisions G19-1 to G19-6 of 2026-11-08, revising D9): what miServer serves as ONE verdict for a behaviour's probe stack, BESIDE the member results, which are unchanged. Exported by miWorkbench from one candidate of a stored blend report (041) with the report's RECORDED parameters; written as RFC 8785 (JCS) after rounding every float to 6 decimals, so two exports of one report are byte-identical. SEMANTICS (pinned by behaviour-verdict-cases.json; per behaviour and window): (1) rule match (any `rules.match.any_of` expression true after the vetoes) -> fires true, decided_by rule_match; a match beats a veto. (2) rule veto (a veto removed a span and nothing matched) suppresses the members whose `veto_applies` is true. (3) the candidate over the members not suppressed: any_of / all_of / k_of_n count members whose OWN served verdict fired, fires when the count >= k (no bar of its own); stack / max / best_single standardise each member's score with params.mean and params.std, then stack = intercept + sum(weights * z), max = max(z), best_single = z[member_index], and fire when value >= threshold (no length bands). (4) an unknown rule (timeout, error, pending operator code, the rule set absent) is no match and no veto; the members decide. (5) a member not armed or that produced nothing: fires true only when a rule or a present member proves it, otherwise fires null with decided_by members_missing, never false. A verdict false while the veto held reads decided_by vetoed. Members bind by detector digest; members_digest = sha256 of the JCS of the sorted detector digests. midataworks-rule-set-v1.json.$comment: Semantics every app implements (feature 016; the cases in rule-signal-cases-v1.json pin each rule). UNITS: every span and offset is in Unicode code points; spans are half-open [start, end); a signal that reads the element has spans in the element. PATTERN DIALECT: RE2 syntax on a subset, RE2 default options: case-sensitive unless ignore_case (Unicode simple case folding: k matches U+212A); '.' does not match newline; ^ and $ match only at the start and end of the text ($ never before a final newline); \d \w \s \b are ASCII and \s is [\t\n\f\r ] (no \v). Refused, naming the rule and the code-point position of the construct: backreference, lookaround, conditional, atomic, possessive, inline_flag, unicode_property, any_byte (\C), repeat_too_large (a count over 1000, or nested counted repeats multiplying past 1000), too_long (over 2000 code points; position 2000), syntax (also: escapes outside \d \D \s \S \w \W \b \B \A \z \a \f \t \n \r \v \0 \xHH and escaped ASCII punctuation; a quantified anchor or boundary; {,n}; (?<name>; repeated group names; '[' inside a class; a class escape or reversed range as a range endpoint). NORMALISATION: text is matched as given; only declared options apply: ignore_case, and fold_fullwidth_ascii (U+FF01-U+FF5E to U+0021-U+007E, U+3000 to U+0020, one to one, applied before matching; substrings come from the original text). SIGNALS: pattern = every non-overlapping match left to right (after a match ending at e the search resumes at e, one code point later when the match was empty). proximity = for each anchor span, the nearest phrase occurrence (literal; word_boundary = ASCII \b on both sides; each phrase matched on its own, so phrases may overlap each other) on the declared side, ignoring a phrase that overlaps the anchor; gap edge to edge (phrase end to anchor start, or anchor end to phrase start) in the declared unit (utf8_bytes = UTF-8 length of the ORIGINAL text between the two spans); ties: smaller gap, then earlier phrase in phrases, then before over after; yields the anchor span with outputs distance, phrase (as written in the text) and side when gap <= max_distance. validator = candidates from the validator's scan, from each span of an earlier signal (value = the span's text, neighbouring text on each side), or from the element; each candidate carries the validator's outputs; the signal FIRES on a candidate only when valid is true, invalid candidates stay readable by field outputs. lexical_weights = one match pass over all terms (longest term first at a position; word_boundary wraps them in ASCII \b); score = sum of the weights of matched terms in text order, each term once under presence and once per match under occurrences; fires when score >= cut; its spans are the first match of each distinct matched term, so count is the number of distinct terms. code_rule = declared only (feature 018). A signal may refer (anchor, span_of) only to an earlier signal. EVALUATION of one row: (1) every signal's spans; (2) vetoes per candidate: each veto's 'when' expression is evaluated on the step-1 spans, then every span of each signal in 'removes' that overlaps a 'when' span (half-open: s1 < e2 and s2 < e1) is removed; vetoed is true when any span was removed; (3) expressions on the remaining spans: signal = true when it has a span, carrying its spans; all = true when every member is true, carrying every member's spans; any = true when some member is true, carrying the true members' spans; not = true when its member is false; within_n(a, b, n, unit) = true when some pair of spans of a and b has gap <= n (edge to edge; overlap is 0), carrying the contributing spans; a false expression and a not carry no spans; carried spans are sorted by start then end without duplicates; (4) outputs: fired = the expression's truth; count = number of carried spans; first = text of the first carried span, else null; spans = canonical JSON [[start, end], ...]; field = the named output of the first remaining candidate of a signal, else null. RENDERINGS, DECOYS, SUBSTITUTIONS are declared and structurally checked here; feature 017 executes renderings and decoys; substitutions are clone parameters (JSON Pointers). RENDERING SEMANTICS (every rendering has normalise(render(v)) == v cases): render builtin spaced = the value's characters joined by one space; split_lines = joined by one newline (U+000A); spelled_out_digits = each ASCII digit 0-9 written as its lower-case English word (zero one two three four five six seven eight nine), every other character kept as itself, the resulting tokens joined by one space; mapping = left to right, at each position the LONGEST key that matches there is replaced by its value, a character no key matches is kept. Normaliser builtin digits_only = keep the ASCII digits 0-9 only; strip_delimiters = remove exactly U+0020 space, U+000A newline, '-' and '.'; words_to_digits = the inverse of spelled_out_digits: read the text as tokens separated by exactly one space, a token that is a digit word becomes its digit and any other token is one kept character; mapping_inverse = the mapping inverted (its values must be distinct), applied the same way (longest key first). IDENTITY: sha256 of the RFC 8785 (JCS) canonical JSON of the document as received (the parsed JSON values before any default; never a re-dump of a model): keys sorted by UTF-16 code units, no whitespace, numbers as values in ECMAScript form (1 and 1.0 are the same number, 1e21 is 1e+21), strings UTF-8 with only the quote, backslash and U+0000-U+001F escaped. An ABSENT list and an EMPTY list differ: an omitted vetoes and vetoes: [] are different documents with different digests. An integer outside +/-(2^53 - 1) is refused (unsafe_integer, naming its JSON Pointer). Strings must be NFC. MATCH (D53): 'match' {version: 1, any_of: [expression names]} states the rule set's POSITIVE: a row (or window) is a rule match when any named expression is true in step (3), after the vetoes; each name is an expression of the document, named once, and never a veto's 'when' expression (refused on save: match_includes_veto_condition, since that veto could then never hold). 'match' is absent or an object, never null. A document WITHOUT 'match' keeps the pre-D53 rule: the positive is every expression an output reads with 'fired' (inferred). BOUNDS (settings, refused naming the setting, never truncated): RULE_SET_MAX_SIGNALS, RULE_SET_MAX_CASES, RULE_SET_MAX_DOCUMENT_BYTES, RULE_SET_MAX_TERMS (lexical terms, default 2000), RULE_SET_MAX_CODE_PARAMS_BYTES (code_rule params, default 16 KiB).

behaviour-verdict-v1.json.description: A behaviour verdict definition (ENH-006 G19, operator decisions G19-1 to G19-6 of 2026-11-08, revising D9): what miServer serves as ONE verdict for a behaviour's probe stack, BESIDE the member results, which are unchanged. Exported by miWorkbench from one candidate of a stored blend report (041) with the report's RECORDED parameters; written as RFC 8785 (JCS) after rounding every float to 6 decimals, so two exports of one report are byte-identical. SEMANTICS (pinned by behaviour-verdict-cases.json; per behaviour and window): (1) rule match (any `rules.match.any_of` expression true after the vetoes) -> fires true, decided_by rule_match; a match beats a veto. (2) rule veto (a veto removed a span and nothing matched) suppresses the members whose `veto_applies` is true. (3) the candidate over the members not suppressed: any_of / all_of / k_of_n count members whose OWN served verdict fired, fires when the count >= k (no bar of its own); stack / max / best_single standardise each member's score with params.mean and params.std, then stack = intercept + sum(weights * z), max = max(z), best_single = z[member_index], and fire when value >= threshold (no length bands). (4) an unknown rule (timeout, error, pending operator code, the rule set absent) is no match and no veto; the members decide. (5) a member not armed or that produced nothing: fires true only when a rule or a present member proves it, otherwise fires null with decided_by members_missing, never false. A verdict false while the veto held reads decided_by vetoed. Members bind by detector digest; members_digest = sha256 of the JCS of the sorted detector digests. A consumer recomputes every combiner vector at attach and refuses on any disagreement (value within 1e-9, everything else exact).

JLensArtifactDocument.description:
Track A: the artifact a consumer MOUNTS (BR-022, PADR IDL-46).

Describes a directory rather than carrying weights. There is no ingestion
API upstream — J-lens is compute-on-demand from a mounted artifact — so a
document that embedded the tensors would be describing a transfer nobody
performs.

ReadoutRecordDocument.description: A position x layer readout, in the upstream wire format (PADR IDL-45).

RecipeProvenance.description:
How an artifact was built (BR-007), carried by every J-space kind.

A document without its recipe cannot be rebuilt or compared, which makes it
an assertion rather than a result.

TemplateLensSpec.description:
Multi-token concepts (BR-023). FIELDS DAY-ONE, compute optional.

The compute path may be a fast-follow; the fields are not. Adding a field to
a shipped kind later is precisely the change BR-021 forbids, so they exist
now and are ABSENT when the path has not run — which is different from zero
and different from unsupported.
